utility.notes: EWEB is a community-owned (municipal) utility, structurally distinct from investor-owned PGE and Pacific Power and from PUC regulation — confirmed directly via EWEB's own site. Not to be assumed for any other Oregon city; each municipal-utility city must be independently verified.

value.name: Eugene Water & Electric Board (EWEB)
value.notes: Per EWEB's own Residential Solar PV Program page: net metering is available up to a maximum system size of 25 kW AC output; excess generation is calculated and trued-up MONTHLY and does NOT roll over to subsequent months (a genuinely distinct policy from many utilities' annual true-up — EWEB explicitly warns that systems sized for a yearly true-up policy 'may be oversized in EWEB service territory'). An alternative 'Direct Generation' rate sells all solar output directly to EWEB rather than net-metering on-site use. EWEB also offers a residential incentive of $0.40 per AC watt (max $2,500), funded by its voluntary Greenpower program, subject to an annually-renewed budget (73% of the $125,000 2026 budget was allocated as of the page's own July 20, 2026 update).

permit_authority.value: City of Eugene, Planning and Development, Building & Permit Services

value.name: EWEB Zero-Interest Backup Power Loan
value.description: Residential loan of up to $5,000 at zero interest for backup power systems, including battery storage; a solar+battery pairing can also provide temporary backup power during outages.
value.eligibility: If a solar system is paired with batteries, the battery must never be able to dispatch onto EWEB's electrical distribution system.

value.name: Roof-mounted: Architect/Engineer design calculations (seismic/wind, snow, and uplift)
value.required_when: only if the system is engineered rather than prescriptive

value.name: Roof-mounted: Roof framing plan (framing members identified, truss/rafter spacing, span)
Roof-mounted: Roof plan showing solar array location/dimensions, roof features (ridges, valleys, chimneys, skylights), roof covering type, and firefighter access pathways
Racking and attachment: manufacturer's spec sheet, attachment locations/spacing, weight
Electric circuits added: number of new circuits, new service or relocated service

Pole-mounted: Site plan (min. 11x17in) with property lines/dimensions, north arrow, scale, adjacent streets/alleys/sidewalks/easements, site elevations/contours, existing and proposed structures with setbacks and distances
Pole-mounted: Structural/footing details, engineering design/calculations, elevations, connections/mounting
EWEB: at least two contractor bids from the Oregon Dept. of Energy approved-contractor list
EWEB: completed Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with supporting documentation, pre-approved by EWEB before installation begins

required_documents.notes: Two independent tracks: the City's own Residential Solar Checklist (Form F-408, updated July 2023) governs the building/roof-mounted or pole-mounted structural permit; EWEB's separate application/PPA process governs interconnection and incentive eligibility. EWEB explicitly requires passing City or County inspection before it will install the interconnection meter.

value: City or County building inspection must pass on the solar installation
After inspection passes and all required documentation is submitted to EWEB, EWEB installs a new (net) meter
EWEB approval is required before the solar system may be energized; EWEB may verify the system for program compliance

timeline_days.notes: EWEB states incentive payments are mailed 'approximately four to six weeks' after EWEB approves the installation, but this is a payment timeline, not a permit-issuance or interconnection-approval timeline, so it was not recorded in this field.

other_conditions: Maximum net-metered system size is 25 kW AC output
Excess generation is trued-up MONTHLY, not annually — systems sized assuming an annual true-up may be oversized for EWEB's territory
Installation must be performed by a contractor on the Oregon Dept. of Energy's Oregon Solar + Storage Rebate Program approved-contractor list to qualify for any EWEB incentive
All PV inverters and battery energy storage systems (including power control systems) must be listed on the California Energy Commission's Solar Equipment List
Project must meet a minimum Total Solar Resource Factor (TSRF) of 85% for incentive qualification only (not required for interconnection itself)
Batteries paired with solar must never be able to dispatch onto EWEB's electrical distribution system
Customers must obtain at least two contractor bids before beginning the application process

permit_fees.notes: The City's Residential Solar Checklist and Solar Submittal Requirements page do not publish a specific solar permit fee; EWEB's page does not charge an interconnection application fee that was stated. Not guessed.

value.name: EWEB Residential Solar Incentive
value.description: Direct cash incentive for residential net-metered solar installations, funded by EWEB's voluntary Greenpower program.
value.eligibility: Must use a contractor on the Oregon Dept. of Energy approved-contractor list; project must meet minimum 85% TSRF; first-come-first-served against an annual budget.

rebates.notes: $0.40/AC watt, maximum $2,500 per project. The page's own July 20, 2026 update states 73% of the $125,000 2026 program budget had already been allocated — this is a live, budget-limited program, not a permanent guarantee, and should be re-verified close to any given customer's application date.
